brief: #140 gave every solid column a cast shadow, and its own surprise was that the binder is the SUN, not the shadow. But there is a second binder it did not name: shTop[] is filled from the eave, and the two tallest drawn things in this town are not eaves. The clock tower reaches z 10.2 and the church spire is higher; both currently throw from eaveBand's 6.3 and 7.8. The tallest volume in the picture casts a terrace's shadow. Give each tower its real height into shTop[] and let the throw be as long as the geometry says. Price the extent off -S/S[2] BEFORE you build, so you know at which hours it is worth anything: sunVec() is a stylised high sun and midday buys almost nothing, but a tower is tall enough that the early and late hours should be dramatic.
successLooksLike: On a clear morning and again in the late afternoon the clock tower lays a shadow down the cross street and the spire one across the far bank's green, long enough to read at Wide and to swing visibly across the hour. Measured against HEAD with a shade-diff on the same seed and instant, with a same-code control.
avoid: Do not touch eaveBand itself - every generic consumer reads it; give the two towers their own entry into shTop[]. Watch the northward veto from #140: a volume lifts ~1.15 rows a cell UP the frame, so an un-vetoed throw paints the caster's own roof, and a tower is exactly where that goes wrong worst. Keep the merged-run fill - overlapping subpaths wind to 2 and double-darken.
